mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over the prior three months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.5% over any 3-month window ending at decision time
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% at decision time
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 6.0% at decision time
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower during triggered events compared to baseline at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months signals supply-side stress, which raises input costs and reduces profit growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month MA for 3 consecutive months ending at decision time
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their prior 12-month averages signals a high-inflation, high-rate environment, which erodes real corporate earnings and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month moving averages at decision time
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower when both proxies exceed their 12-month averages at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A strong rebound in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) above its prior 4-quarter average, combined with a decline in the mortgage rate proxy (HOUST), signals improved household purchasing power and housing affordability, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > 4-quarter average AND HOUST < prior 4-quarter average at decision time
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during co-occurrence of both triggers at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer demand and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month MA for 4 consecutive months ending at decision time
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during triggered labor expansion episodes at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) below its 6-month moving average signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces revenue growth for consumer-facing firms and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 6-month MA for 2 consecutive months ending at decision time
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes at 5% significance.
